name: ProxyMIR Reseller Storefront
author: ProxyMIR

sections.description:
ProxyMIR Reseller Storefront connects your WordPress site to the ProxyMIR.com proxy service as a partner (reseller). Visitors of your site open a shop widget, choose a package, register, pay and receive their proxies. The service takes care of the proxies, the payments and the buyers’ accounts; the plugin shows the shop on your site and the partner area in your dashboard.

What you get

  • A shop widget in a phone-style window: catalog, personal area, reviews, top up, proxy checker. Light and dark theme, position and logo of the button are set in the plugin.
  • Your own markup on top of the service price (up to 100%) and live earnings statistics: income, orders, traffic sold, top products, payout history.
  • Payout requests to a Bitcoin address of your choice, handled by the service.
  • News from the service and a support desk (tickets with the service administrators) inside your dashboard.
  • English and Russian interface; every dashboard user picks the language with the flags in the plugin header.

You need a partner account

The plugin is a client of an external service and does nothing useful without a partner account at ProxyMIR.com. When you press Connect to ProxyMIR.com on the first screen, the plugin creates the partner account and the API key for your site, and all sections open at once. If the service asks for an application first, you fill in a short form (name, job title, site, email) and the sections open when it is approved. Details are on the first screen of the plugin and at https://proxymir.com/index.php/reseller/.

The plugin makes no request to the service until the site administrator presses Connect to ProxyMIR.com on the first screen.

External services

This plugin is a client of the ProxyMIR.com service (https://proxymir.com), which is operated by the plugin author. All shop logic, prices, accounts, payments and payouts live on that service; the plugin sends requests to it.

  • Terms of the service: https://proxymir.com/index.php/terms/?lang=en
  • Privacy policy of the service: https://proxymir.com/index.php/privacy/?lang=en

When the plugin contacts the service

  • Only after the site administrator pressed “Connect to ProxyMIR.com”, or when an API key or an application is already saved.
  • When you press “Connect to ProxyMIR.com” and the service takes partners without an application, the partner account is created at once (site address, administrator email and interface language are sent, the API key comes back and is saved).
  • When you open the plugin screens in the dashboard (offer, connection, statistics, news, support), when you save the settings, send an application, create or change the key, request a payout or write to support.
  • On the public site, when a visitor uses the shop widget (registers, logs in, orders, pays, asks for proxies, writes to support). The request goes from the visitor’s browser to your own site, and the plugin forwards it to the service. In the background the plugin refreshes the shop catalog (about every five minutes) and, in the dashboard, news and tickets.

What is sent

  • With every request: the plugin version, the API key (when one exists) and the site address.
  • When an API key is created: the site address, the site administrator email and the interface language.
  • When an application is sent: the name, job title, site and email typed into the form.
  • For shop visitors: what the visitor types into the widget (login, email, password, orders, messages to support) and the visitor’s IP address and browser name, which the service uses for abuse protection. For sites behind Cloudflare the visitor address is taken from the Cloudflare header.
  • Cookie: after a visitor logs in to the shop widget the plugin sets one functional cookie, prxr_buyer (HttpOnly, up to 30 days), with the session of the visitor. The site administrator’s browser gets no cookie from the plugin.
  • Payment: when a buyer pays, the widget opens the payment page of the payment provider chosen by the service. The plugin itself never sees card data.

The plugin adds a ready-made paragraph to Settings > Privacy (the privacy policy guide) that describes this.

Links the user can click

  • The payout history links to https://mempool.space (a public Bitcoin explorer) for the transaction of a paid payout. Nothing is sent to it unless the user clicks the link.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open ProxyMIR Reseller in the dashboard menu, read the offer and press Connect to ProxyMIR.com. If you already have a key from another site, open “Already have a key?” on the same screen and paste it instead.
  3. The partner account is created and Statistics, Settings, News and Support open. If the service asks for an application, send it first; when it is approved, press Create API key in Settings.
  4. In ProxyMIR Reseller > Settings set your markup, the look of the button and the language of the widget.
  5. Put the shortcode [proxy_reseller] on any page (a floating button) or [proxy_reseller inline="1" width="300" height="120"] where the button should appear inside the content.
sections.faq:
Is the plugin free?

Yes. The plugin is free and open source. Selling through the service means you earn a share of every sale; the service terms are at https://proxymir.com/index.php/terms/?lang=en.

Where is my API key stored?

In a separate option, encrypted with libsodium (XSalsa20-Poly1305) with a key derived from the salts of your wp-config.php. If the salts change, the key cannot be read any more and the plugin asks you to enter the saved key again. Save the key when it is shown.

Does the plugin store card or wallet data?

No. Payments are made on the pages of the payment providers; the BTC address for payouts is stored in the plugin settings and checked by the service.

Can I use another server?

Operators of their own compatible service can define PRXR_HUB_URL in wp-config.php (or use the prxr_hub_url filter).

How do I stop the plugin from contacting the service?

Open ProxyMIR Reseller > Settings > Connection and press “Withdraw permission”. The plugin stops all requests to the service and the shop window disappears from the site. Your key and settings are kept; the button “Connect to ProxyMIR.com” turns everything on again.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

All plugin data (settings, the encrypted key, caches, per-user settings) is removed from your database. Your partner account at the service is not affected.
sections.changelog:
2.1.5

  • If the plugin is installed next to its former copy (folder proxy-reseller), the second copy no longer causes a fatal error on activation: it stays idle and shows a notice.

2.1.4

  • The plugin is renamed to ProxyMIR Reseller Storefront (new plugin folder and text domain). Settings and the saved API key are kept.

2.1.3

  • Widget header: the large title no longer flickers on short screens (for example a single result in the proxy checker).

2.1.2

  • Payment screen: when the service takes a payment gateway in US dollars, the amount is shown in dollars instead of being left out.

2.1.1

  • Buyer-facing errors from the service (top-up limits, crypto top-up, payment gateway, checkout, reviews) are now shown in the language of the widget. Before, some of them appeared in Russian on English pages.

2.1.0

  • First screen: the second “Connect” button under the offer is gone. The single button “Connect to ProxyMIR.com” now also creates the partner account when the service takes partners without an application, and Statistics, Settings, News and Support open at once.
  • “Already have a key?” is available on the first screen for partners who move the plugin to another site.

2.0.9

  • The built-in offer text in Russian was rewritten to match the English one.

2.0.8

  • English interface texts use plain quotes and “>” in menu paths. No change in behaviour.

2.0.7

  • The data blocks of the Statistics and Settings screens are printed with wp_print_inline_script_tag() instead of a hand-written script tag. Nothing changes on the screens.

2.0.6

  • Readme: the plugin author account.

2.0.5

  • The shop visitor’s session cookie is now added next to the cookies of other plugins instead of replacing them.
  • The request limit of the visitor relay counts an IPv6 visitor by the /64 network, so changing the last part of the address no longer avoids the limit.
  • The built-in offer text was rewritten: correct step numbers and a plain description of how payouts work.
  • The “Clear plugin cache” button now says what it really does: it clears only the data the plugin keeps itself (earlier the hint named other plugins’ caches).
  • Settings texts no longer call the service “Hub”; the strings meant for the dashboard are no longer sent to the public pages.
  • Uninstall also removes the short request counters of the relay.

2.0.4

  • Readme: the plugin author account.

2.0.3

  • The login session of a shop visitor is no longer kept in the browser storage. The plugin keeps it in one HttpOnly cookie (prxr_buyer, SameSite=Strict) and adds it to the requests itself, so a script on the page cannot read it. Requests that come from a page of another site are refused.
  • New button “Withdraw permission” (ProxyMIR Reseller > Settings > Connection): the plugin stops contacting the service and the shop window is switched off; the key and the settings are kept, one button connects again.
  • Links to the Terms and the Privacy Policy open their English version.

2.0.2

  • Security review. The shop relay for visitors now limits the size of a request and the number of requests from one address, never answers with a 5xx status, and tells caches not to keep its replies.
  • The plugin reads at most 4 MB from the service in one reply.
  • The visitor address handed to the service can be set with the prxr_visitor_ip filter (sites behind a proxy other than Cloudflare); the request limit can be changed with prxr_buyer_rate_limit.
  • The decision on an application is asked for only on the plugin’s own screens, never during AJAX or on other plugins’ screens.
  • Background tasks are removed on deactivation; on a multisite network every site is cleaned on deletion.
  • Language switch of the shop window works from the keyboard; the window has a name for screen readers.

2.0.1

  • Removed unused code and texts (no change in behaviour).

2.0.0

  • First release in the WordPress.org directory. Earlier 1.x versions were distributed privately.
  • No self-update: updates come from WordPress.org.
  • The plugin contacts the service only after the administrator pressed “Connect”, and adds a paragraph to the privacy policy guide.
  • Scripts and styles are enqueued through WordPress; the widget files are plain, readable source.
  • The plugin no longer clears caches of other plugins.

short_description: Storefront widget for the ProxyMIR.com proxy service: offer proxy traffic on your site, follow your earnings and request payouts.
